text:
lina: FYI I ran a 1F1B sweep on 8xA100 this morning, saw recurring ~10-14ms all-reduce spikes every ~120 steps when microbatch=2 and seq_len tail is heavy. putting logs + a tiny flame link here :eyes:
perf-bot: perf summary uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/reports/2187654321/flame.html — mean allreduce 2.3ms, p95 13.7ms, pp-step-latency variance up 18%
mike: interesting — could be kernel selection falling back to non-fused path under small msg sizes. try forcing fused allreduce kernels or toggle NCCL algo to compare. also check /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_congestion_control on hosts.
arjun: also suspicious of KV cache thrash: when microbatch small we do more KV lookups per step and prefetch timing may collide with comm windows. try kv_prefetch=1 and bump microbatch to 4 to amortize.
samira: small tweak we've used before: introduce a tight 1F1B interleave gap (onef1b_delay_ms) to let comm start earlier and overlap more. mocha run command I used below — keeps seq/prefetch timing more stable:
```
python perf/run.py --model gpt-j-6B --pp 2 --tp 2 --microbatch 4 --onef1b_delay_ms 2 --kv_prefetch 1 --force-kernel allreduce_fused
```

lina: can you paste the tiny log excerpt of the spike? seeing pattern would help.
arjun: log snip (step boundary times):
```
[step 120] compute 18.2ms | allreduce 2.1ms | kv-prefetch 0.8ms
[step 121] compute 18.0ms | allreduce 13.4ms | kv-prefetch 1.0ms  <-- spike
[step 122] compute 17.9ms | allreduce 2.0ms | kv-prefetch 0.9ms
```
mike: that looks like occasional serialization in NCCL collective; try setting NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 and test NCCL_ALGO=ring vs tree. also run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to get timestamps.
perf-bot: queued a microbatch sweep job (job id 2187654321-01) with knobs: microbatch=[2,4], onef1b_delay_ms=[0,1,2,5], kv_prefetch=[0,1,2], kernel_override=[auto,allreduce_fused]. results will be under artifacts link when done.
deploy-bot: ci artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal/artifacts/2187654321-01 — logs, flamegraphs, nvprof traces.
lina: thanks — i'll let it run overnight. plan: try mike's NCCL knobs + samira's delay + arjun's kv_prefetch. will post numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
mike: if spike persists, try increasing microbatch further or switch to a different kernel selection policy (prefers-suba llreduce for mid-size msgs). also check host NIC interrupts — we had one case where IRQ balancing caused jitter.
samira: fyi when we used onef1b_delay_ms=2 previously we dropped p95 bubble by ~30% on similar model. small but consistent.
lina: good to know. will report back. :party:
